I'm not sure what you mean. It is nice to have the support of your partner, family, friends, etc. However, no one's success should depend on another person. That's an incredibly weak position to be in.

As for the original question, I prefer honesty. People should have their own mind, thoughts, feelings. That doesn't mean you should be a dick and make your partner look like a fool in front of a bunch of people. There are polite ways to disagree. Or, you can choose not say anything at all.

I think both partners should support each other. Lying to protect your partner's image, or ego... that's pseudo-support, to me. I don't think it will really help them grow as a person.

Of course, all of this is up to the people in the relationship themselves. Only they can decide what their roles should or shouldn't be. However, I don't think this should be the default standard for all women or men.

Unfortunately this kind of rhetorical question is very situational.

It's like asking ' do the ends justify the means? ' in some circumstances, ABSOLUTELY. In others, of course not. If the means were 5 million people died from inhumane drug testing to cure a disease that only impacts a few thousand people, then no. If someone tackles a suicide bomber, sacrificing their own life but saving dozens of others, then yes. In this way neither question is very fair.

Overall though your husband/wife is your partner, your teammate, your confidant. Disagreements should usually be handled behind closed doors whenever possible. You should never try to humiliate or undermine your partner unless it's pretty serious. If the partner says "sure, I can drive! I've only had 13 beers!" Obviously there is no time to wait until you're home, you need to stop that sort of thing immediately. But if your husband/wife is pretending to like football in the middle of a business meeting with potential clients, don't undercut your partner by calling them out in front of the associates. Wait until you're in the car together to say you can't wait to watch football on Sunday.

It's a bit of a poor set of examples, but I hope anyone reading this understands the gist of it.
The way the question is asked...Sheesh!! I think that where possible, both partners should support each other, even to the extent of saving face, but not to the extent of harming someone else.
